Tyler: hey folks quick q — need to bump lodash from 4.17.21 -> 4.17.22 in infra-configs. what's the preferred branch pattern + commit msg style for tiny dep updates? do I need a changelog entry?
Olivia: branch off main. name it deps/lodash-4.17.22 or chore/deps/lodash-4.17.22 (we use either, keep it short). commit msg: chore(deps): bump lodash 4.17.21 -> 4.17.22. no changelog for internal dev deps unless it affects users.
Mira: also check CODEOWNERS for the package — if infra-configs has /infra/* owned by @infra-team add them as reviewer. if it touches runtime images or build containers ping me. we don't create hotfix branches for normal dependency bumps unless it's a security/urgent fix.
Ben (eng): run the usual local checks before pushing:
```bash
git checkout -b deps/lodash-4.17.22
npm ci
npm run lint && npm run test
# or for monorepo: pnpm -w -r test
```
Olivia: include the automated lockfile change in the same PR. If Dependabot created it, prefix the PR with "dependabot" in the title so release tooling can skip it when necessary. If the bump requires a minor code tweak, keep the change scoped and add a tiny unit test.
Mira: reviewers — add @infra-team and one person from the owning service (check CODEOWNERS), and mark the PR as "chore" label. We prefer 1 approving reviewer for non-prod-impact changes, 2 for anything touching runtime.
ci-bot: CI queued — build 12788 (lint/test) for deps/lodash-4.17.22, status: pending.
Tyler: awesome thanks! i'll open deps/lodash-4.17.22 with the chore commit msg and add infra-team as reviewer. will ping if CI flakes. :thumbsup:
Olivia: one more nit — use imperative verb in PR title e.g. "Bump lodash to 4.17.22" so changelog tools read it correctly.
Tyler: noted, thanks everyone :)
